Before you bid / private browser tool

Is this tender ready for your attention?

Paste the solicitation text. Get a practical checklist of the details that can make a bid ineligible or waste a week of preparation.


Nothing is uploaded. The check runs on this device.

Common questions

Does a 100% score mean the tender is safe to bid?

No. It means all seven readiness signals (deadline, bond, insurance, certification, mandatory pre-bid meeting or site visit, submission channel, questions/addenda) were found as phrases somewhere in the text you pasted — it is a keyword match, not a reading of whether the requirement is satisfiable or reasonable. Green means the phrase was found, not that the requirement is met, and the tool says so on screen.

Why does it say a signal was “not found” when I know the tender mentions it?

The checker looks for specific wording patterns (like "due", "deadline", "bid bond", "certificate of insurance") within 100 characters of a match; a solicitation that only discusses a requirement in an attachment, an addendum, or unusual phrasing won't be caught by these patterns. Always read the original document and any addenda yourself — the tool tells you this in its own warnings.

Does this replace reading the actual solicitation and attachments?

No. This is a heuristic first pass to flag what to look for before you spend hours preparing a bid, not a substitute for reading the full solicitation, its attachments, and any addenda. It is not legal or procurement advice.

Is the tender text I paste uploaded anywhere?

No. The check runs entirely in your browser against the text you paste; nothing is sent to a server. Only anonymous local usage counts are kept, and you can turn that off with the checkbox in the footer.

should-i-bid-on-this-tender.html.text:
← Tender bid readiness checker

Should I bid on this tender?

A small contractor's expensive mistake is not bidding too low. It is spending a full day pricing a public contract and then failing on something that was in the notice all along — a bond that takes two weeks to arrange, an insurance limit above the policy in the drawer, a clarification window that closed on Tuesday.

The go/no-go is a paperwork decision, and it is answerable in ten minutes before any estimating time is spent.

Open the free bid readiness checker

The six things to find before you price anything

  • Two deadlines, not one. The submission deadline is the one everyone reads. The deadline for clarification questions is usually earlier, and once it passes, anything ambiguous in the scope stays ambiguous and becomes your risk.
  • Bonds. A bid bond, performance bond, or payment bond is a relationship with a surety, not a form. If you do not already have a facility, "we need one by Friday" is frequently the end of the conversation.
  • Insurance limits. Not whether you have cover — whether your limits meet the stated minimums, and whether the buyer must be named as an additional insured.
  • Licences and certifications. Trade licences, registrations, quality or safety certifications, and any prequalification scheme the buyer requires membership of.
  • Addenda and mandatory site visits. An unacknowledged addendum voids bids on many public contracts, and a mandatory pre-bid visit that has already taken place cannot be recovered.
  • The submission channel. Portal upload, sealed hard copy, or email to a named address, and whose clock the deadline runs on. A compliant bid delivered the wrong way is a non-compliant bid.

How to use the checker

  1. Paste the notice text into the tool. Nothing is uploaded — the check runs in your browser.
  2. Select Check readiness. Each finding keeps a short excerpt of the text it matched.
  3. Open the source document at each excerpt and confirm it. The excerpt is a pointer, not a finding of fact.
  4. Turn anything you cannot satisfy in the time available into a no-go, and stop there.

The checker is deliberately heuristic. It does not fetch portals, upload text, judge eligibility, or submit anything.

Why "no" is a result worth ten minutes

A contractor who prices four tenders a month and wins one has spent three days on losses. Filtering out the two that were never winnable on paperwork returns two of those days to work that pays — and leaves more time for the one bid that was genuinely worth the effort.

Common questions

Should I bid on this tender?

Decide the paperwork question before the pricing question. Read the notice for the submission deadline and the separate — usually earlier — deadline for clarification questions, then for bonds, insurance limits, licences or certifications, and the exact channel the bid must arrive through. If any of those is something you cannot satisfy in the time available, the bid is a no-go regardless of how well the work suits you, and you have saved a day of estimating.

What disqualifies a small contractor most often?

Administrative failures rather than price: a bid bond or performance bond the contractor cannot obtain at short notice, insurance limits below the stated minimum, a missing licence or certification, a mandatory site visit that has already happened, an unanswered addendum, or a submission sent through the wrong channel or arriving after the stated clock. These are all knowable from the notice before any estimating time is spent.

Does this tool decide whether I am eligible?

No. It is a deterministic text checker that highlights common signals and keeps a short evidence excerpt for each one so you can return to the source. A phrase it did not find is not proof the requirement is absent, and a phrase it did find is not proof your business qualifies. Read the original tender, every attachment, and every addendum before deciding.

No warranty. This free page is not legal, procurement, financial, or insurance advice, and it does not determine whether you are eligible to bid or whether a bid is compliant. It is a heuristic reading aid. Read the original tender, its attachments, and every addendum, and verify every requirement with the buyer and a qualified professional before relying on it or submitting. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for loss or damage arising from its use.

vs-govwin.html.text:
← Tender bid readiness checker

This checker vs. GovWin IQ

Two different jobs: GovWin IQ, from Deltek, is an account-based government-contracting intelligence platform for finding public-sector opportunities and tracking who else bids on them. This page is a free, private readiness pass on one tender you already have, before you spend a day pricing it.

Open the free bid readiness checker

What each tool is for

GovWin IQ is a government-contracting intelligence platform built by Deltek for contractors who sell into the public sector: opportunity discovery and forecasting, incumbent and competitor tracking, agency spending history, and market research, run as an ongoing account. GovWin IQ's own pricing and current feature list are not reachable from this session to confirm, so no dollar figure or plan name for GovWin IQ is invented here: only its well-documented identity and category — an account-based public-sector opportunity and competitive-intelligence platform — are stated.

This checker does none of what GovWin IQ does. It does not find opportunities, forecast agency spending, or track competitors. It takes the text of one solicitation you paste in and scans it for seven readiness signals — deadline, bid or performance bond, insurance limits, licences or certifications, a mandatory pre-bid meeting or site visit, the submission channel, and open questions or addenda — entirely in your browser, with no account and nothing uploaded.

Where to answer each question.
QuestionWhere to answer it
I need to find public-sector opportunities and see who else usually bids on them.GovWin IQ, or a comparable platform — opportunity discovery is not something this checker does.
I already have a notice. Is it worth a day of pricing time before I check the paperwork?This checker — free, instant, private, no account.
What deadlines, bonds, insurance, licences, and site-visit requirements does this specific notice list?This checker's readiness report, with an evidence excerpt for each finding.
How has this agency awarded similar contracts in the past?GovWin IQ, or a comparable research platform — this checker reads only the notice you paste in.
Do I need to create an account or sign up to use the tool?This checker: no. GovWin IQ is used through a Deltek account.

Most public-sector contractors get different value from each: GovWin IQ (or a comparable platform) for finding and forecasting opportunities as an ongoing account, and a private checker like this one for an instant, no-login readiness pass once a specific notice is already in hand. This page's own findings are a paperwork-risk pointer, not a market forecast or a competitor record.

Common questions

Should I use this checker or GovWin IQ?

Both, for different jobs, and a contractor who already subscribes to GovWin IQ to find opportunities can still paste a found notice into this checker before spending a day pricing it. GovWin IQ, from Deltek, is a government-contracting intelligence platform: opportunity discovery and forecasting, incumbent and competitor tracking, and agency spending research, run as an ongoing account. This checker does none of that. It takes the text of one solicitation you already have and scans it for seven readiness signals — deadline, bond, insurance, certification, mandatory pre-bid meeting or site visit, submission channel, and questions or addenda — entirely in your browser, with no account and nothing uploaded. A contractor who needs to find and forecast public-sector opportunities is better served by GovWin IQ or a comparable platform; a contractor who already has a notice in hand and wants a fast, free, private first pass at its paperwork risk is in the right place here.

Does GovWin IQ check a tender for the readiness signals this tool looks for?

GovWin IQ's own research and alerts can surface an opportunity and its agency history, but reading one solicitation's own bond, insurance, and deadline requirements is not that platform's job any more than it is this checker's job to find the opportunity in the first place. Some contractors will use GovWin IQ or a comparable service to find and shortlist notices, then run each shortlisted notice through this free checker before committing estimating time; neither tool replaces the other.

Is this page affiliated with GovWin IQ?

No. This site is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Deltek, Inc. or GovWin IQ. GovWin IQ is a trademark of its owner, named here only to describe what this checker is and is not.
